paper: Lohani, Hickey, Masell & Rosch, Quantum skyrmions in frustrated ferromagnets, PRX 9, 041063 (2019); arXiv:1901.03343
replication_verdict: REPLICATED (core ED claim + quantitative Cperp anchor); Coverage ~6-7/10, Agreement ~8/10

open_questions.question: Does the quantum skyrmion's exponentially small bandwidth, arising from skyrmion<->antiskyrmion tunneling, reproduce in an independent ED build?
open_questions.why_heavy: This is the paper's headline DYNAMICAL result (abstract: 'bandwidth is exponentially small and arises from tunneling processes between skyrmion and antiskyrmion'). It requires resolving a tunneling splitting that is exponentially small in system size/barrier, demanding either full spectra (not just the ground state per sector) with high relative precision, or a constructed effective two-state (skyrmion/antiskyrmion) model. eigsh(k=1) as used here cannot see it.
open_questions.compute_estimate: Full or many-lowest-state ED on the 19-31 site flakes with resolved near-degenerate doublets; needs shift-invert eigsh(sigma=...) and careful degeneracy handling. Days of build + run.
open_questions.blocked_by: Effective helicity/tunneling model not built; need eigsh spectra with k>1 and degeneracy resolution.

open_questions.question: Do the angular-momentum quantum numbers l_z lock to the spin quantum number N_f as the paper claims ('locking of angular momentum and spin quantum numbers characteristic for skyrmions')?
open_questions.why_heavy: Requires building the C6 (or C3) point-group rotation operator on the flake, block-diagonalizing each fixed-Sz sector by its l_z eigenvalue, and tracking how the ground-state l_z shifts by a fixed increment each time N_f changes by one. This is a symmetry-resolved ED, substantially more code than the plain sector sweep, and the flake must have exact rotational symmetry (the round flakes are only approximately round).
open_questions.compute_estimate: Symmetry-adapted basis construction + projected diagonalization per (Sz, l_z) block. Moderate: ~1-2 days.
open_questions.blocked_by: No rotation-symmetry operator implemented; flake geometry needs exact C6.

open_questions.question: What is the full J2-B (and J2-K) phase diagram, and where exactly is the skyrmion-stable region boundary (paper Fig. 4, J2 >~ 0.45)?
open_questions.why_heavy: Requires a 2D parameter sweep of the binding-energy criterion and Cperp across (J2, B) or (J2, K), at fixed large flake size, with a clear order parameter for 'skyrmion present'. Each grid point is a full multi-sector ED; a converged phase boundary needs a fine grid and the larger flake to avoid finite-size smearing of the transition.
open_questions.compute_estimate: O(100s) of ED runs (grid x sectors) on 19-31 site flakes. Embarrassingly parallel; ~hours on nuc13/Crux if parallelized, but a real build.
open_questions.blocked_by: Only three (J2,K) points computed; no systematic sweep or phase-boundary extraction.

open_questions.question: Does the winding-number correlation (paper Eq. 12, the arctan of transverse spin-spin correlations) yield the expected quantized-in-the-classical-limit winding for the bound state?
open_questions.why_heavy: We used the maximal transverse anticorrelation Cperp as a proxy anchor, but the paper's actual topological diagnostic is the arctan winding-correlation summed around real-space loops. Building it requires the full set of two-point transverse correlators <Si+ Sj-> for all pairs, reconstruction of a real-space texture/phase field, and the loop-winding integral - and interpreting a necessarily non-integer quantum winding. This is the quantum-vs-classical winding comparison that motivates the whole paper.
open_questions.compute_estimate: Full correlation-matrix extraction (already partly in code) + winding reconstruction. Moderate build: ~1-2 days.
open_questions.blocked_by: Eq. 12 arctan winding form not implemented; only max-pair Cperp computed.

open_questions.question: Do the finite-flake results converge to the thermodynamic-limit skyrmion as flake size grows (7 -> 19 -> 31 -> larger), i.e. is the bound state a genuine localized object rather than a finite-size artifact?
open_questions.why_heavy: The paper uses up to 31 sites; we reached 19. Establishing that E0B(Nf), the droplet size, and Cperp converge (rather than drift) with flake size is the finite-size-scaling argument that upgrades 'negative binding on a small flake' to 'genuine localized skyrmion'. The 31-site sector dimensions (e.g. C(31,6)=736k, C(31,10)=44M) push eigsh into needing careful memory management and possibly Lanczos on a matrix-free operator.
open_questions.compute_estimate: 31-site flake, Nf up to ~10: largest sectors are tens of millions of states -> matrix-free eigsh or a bigger-memory host (nuc13 62GB or uicgpu). ~days including build.
open_questions.blocked_by: 31-site flake not built; needs matrix-free H action and a larger-memory compute target.

next_steps: Build the 31-site round flake with a matrix-free eigsh operator (LinearOperator applying H on the fly) to avoid storing the sparse matrix for the largest Sz sectors; run on nuc13 (62GB) or uicgpu.
Implement the C6 rotation operator and symmetry-adapt each Sz sector into l_z blocks to test the angular-momentum/spin locking (Q2).
Implement the paper's Eq. 12 arctan winding-correlation from the full transverse two-point correlator set already accessible in lohani_ed.py (Q4).
Add shift-invert eigsh(k>1, sigma=E0) to resolve the near-degenerate skyrmion/antiskyrmion doublet and estimate the tunneling bandwidth (Q1).
Parallelize a (J2, B) grid of binding + Cperp runs (embarrassingly parallel) to map the phase boundary against paper Fig. 4 (Q3).
